name: Dorfromantik - Perfect Placement scoring & chime
one_line: Tile that matches all 6 edges triggers a distinctive audio chime plus a 60-point bonus and an extra tile added to your draw stack
take_what: A single sharp, distinct sound effect reserved ONLY for the rarest best-case placement (perfect 6-side match), contrasted against otherwise calm ambient audio, PLUS a tangible reward (extra card/tile) not just points

name: Dorfromantik - retroactive perfect-fit double-scoring
one_line: If a later tile placement completes a previously-imperfect neighbor into a perfect 6-match, BOTH the new tile's placement points AND the 60-point perfect bonus fire retroactively
take_what: Scoring resolves not just for the tile placed but re-checks and rewards neighbors that just became 'complete' as a side effect - creates a cascade/chain-reaction feeling from one placement

name: Dorfromantik - quest tiles as demands placed ON the board
one_line: Objectives (e.g. 'close a forest region of 15 tiles', 'deer needs 3 connected forest tiles') are physical tokens sitting on specific hexes on the board itself, not a sidebar checklist
take_what: Bind the goal state to a literal board location so the player's eye and hand are pulled toward it while placing - the quest IS the map, not a UI panel next to the map

name: Dorfromantik - core-interaction-must-feel-good design philosophy (Timo Falcke interview)
one_line: Toukana's stated design rule: 'the interaction the player does the most has to feel as satisfying as possible' - drove them to add tiny animations and sound to every single tile placement, the one action repeated hundreds of times per run
take_what: Audit the single most-repeated player action in Limen (placing a tile) and guarantee it alone - not just wins/captures - has a satisfying micro-animation + sound cue on every placement, independent of whether it does anything strategically

name: ISLANDERS - translucent radius preview sphere before placing
one_line: When you pick up a building to place, a translucent sphere appears around the cursor showing exactly which existing buildings/terrain are within scoring range before you commit
take_what: Show the influence radius as a live overlay attached to the cursor/ghost tile DURING placement (not after), so the player sees which enemy/friendly tiles will be affected before committing - directly attacks Limen's 'placement lacks strategic feeling even though math exists' problem

name: ISLANDERS - asymmetric proximity scoring table (Score & Strategy Bible)
one_line: Every building has its own idiosyncratic proximity rule table: Sawmill +7 per nearby Lumberjack but -12 per nearby Sawmill; Temple near Market is -20; only specific pairs synergize while same-type clustering is punished
take_what: Make same-tile-type stacking/clustering actively punished for SOME tile types (not universal +N per neighbor) so players can't just blob one card everywhere - forces spatial variety and creates 'aha this pair is great together' discovery moments
constraint: needs careful balance pass per card

name: ISLANDERS - session ends when no legal high-value placement remains (soft, player-declared finish)
one_line: No turn limit or clock - the island 'runs out' when no more points can be gained because inventory or space is exhausted, and the player chooses when to sail to the next island
take_what: Anti-pattern for Limen specifically: an open-ended, player-paced end condition is what CAUSES slow corner-building in city-builders - it works for solitaire ISLANDERS precisely because there's no opponent to race. Confirms Limen needs a hard pressure mechanism (rift drain, capital timer) that ISLANDERS deliberately omits.
constraint: none - this is a negative lesson, not a mechanic to port

name: ISLANDERS - two-choice building-pack unlock at point thresholds
one_line: On hitting a score threshold, player picks ONE of two offered building-pack themes (e.g. farming vs fishing) to unlock next, permanently shaping what's available for the rest of that island
take_what: A binary draft choice at milestones (pick pack A or B) that locks in a build direction - could map to Limen deck construction as a small in-run drafting layer to address 'decks feel thin', letting players branch mid-run rather than only pre-game deckbuild
constraint: changes core deckbuilding model - would need play-testing to see if it fits Limen's fixed 20-card deck format

name: Dorfromantik - five quest-tile subtypes with escalating structure (Number+, Number, Number+Triangle, Flag, Crown)
one_line: Quests aren't one generic type - they range from lenient ('reach at least N') to strict ('reach exactly N then seal the region') to meta (Crown quests that unlock further quest chains), each worth different flat point values (100 for closing a quest, 50 for closing a flag)
take_what: A taxonomy of objective-tile difficulty (loose threshold vs exact-count-then-seal vs chained meta-objective) with flat, predictable point payouts rather than scaling formulas - gives players legible short-term goals distinct from the long-game influence math
